section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Solving Equations and Inequalities with Absolute Value

title: Solve |ax + b| <= c (one interval)
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §2.7 pp. 162-163 (CC BY 4.0): method only
process_card: Solving an absolute value inequality with less than

problem.prompt: Solve and write the solution set in interval notation: {tex:absx} \le {tex:cd}

steps.name: write it as a double inequality
solve the double inequality for x
write the answer in interval notation

mistakes.name: wrote two pieces (that is for greater than)
mistakes.message: |X| < c means -c < X < c: one interval between the two numbers.

mistakes.name: wrong bracket type
mistakes.message: < and > leave the endpoints out: ( ). ≤ and ≥ include them: [ ].

hints.hint: Add the number subtracted outside the bars to both sides.
hints.why: The rule works only on |X| compared with c.

hints.step: write it as a double inequality
hints.why: Less than c units from 0 means between -c and c.

hints.step: solve the double inequality for x
hints.hint: Do the same thing to all three parts; dividing by a negative reverses both signs.
hints.why: That keeps all three parts true.

hints.step: write the answer in interval notation
